expected.contract: Canonical PR body sections must match the active body contract before publish or replay.

observed.drift: Historical PRs may retain non-canonical sections such as a duplicated Development Link section or invalid Links rows.
observed.why_it_blocks: The expected body shape is contract-owned, so publish/apply must stop until the contract breach is corrected or a canonical rewrite source is prepared.

samples.next_action: Correct the contract breach first; do not treat canonical-section drift as an apply-time guessable repair.

expected.github_surface: Trailing close-link footer lines such as Closes #309

observed.drift: Metadata could show Development issue without GitHub closingIssuesReferences or full deterministic PR labels.
observed.repair_mode: Replayable through deterministic derive, bounded PR body rewrite/apply, label backfill, and post-apply verify.

samples.next_action: Emit deterministic close-link rows and missing labels into a bounded replay manifest, then re-fetch live PR state.

expected.quality_bar: Readable 3-5 sentence Context prose with no placeholders and a clear outcome sentence.

observed.drift: Context wording may be awkward, stale, or still too template-shaped while remaining structurally valid.
observed.why_not_replayable: Prose quality is not a deterministic field and should not be batch-guessed during remediation.

samples.next_action: Surface the drift as manual work and keep it outside replay/apply batches.

expected.source_of_truth: Explicit links.issue / links.pr rows in the source log must agree with live GitHub references.
expected.apply_policy: No overwrite when both sides are explicit and conflicting.

observed.drift: If a source-log issue URL or explicit issue reference conflicts with live issue identity, replay must stop before any body, relationship, or write-back mutation.
observed.why_it_stops: The mismatch is not a missing field but a competing explicit claim about ownership or identity.

samples.next_action: Require operator resolution of the winning reference and then regenerate deterministic expectations from the corrected source.
